summary: The diff handed to this review was only a 23-line status update in a plan-tracking YAML file, not real code, so per the standing rule against trusting self-reports I pulled the real PR (github.com/FChecklist/compliance-tracker#558) and reviewed the actual code: it extracts the duplicated x-forwarded-for/x-real-ip IP-extraction logic into src/lib/utils/request-ip.ts and the duplicated Supabase admin-client construction into src/lib/supabase/admin-client.ts (a lazily-validated singleton with a named SupabaseAdminConfigError replacing a bare non-null assertion), then wires both into failure-event/route.ts, passcode-login/route.ts, and sso/[orgSlug]/acs/route.ts. Both extractions are behavior-preserving (each call site's own fallback -- undefined vs 'unknown' -- is kept at the call site, not baked into the shared helper) and are backed by real, correctly-targeted unit tests. The change is additive/refactor-only with no schema, migration, or workflow-file changes; PR CI is green on Lint, Type Check, Unit Tests, Build, and Secret/Security scanning, and now merged main -- the only two red checks (Metadata Index Coverage Check and audit-check) are unrelated to this diff: the former already fails on main itself for an unrelated pre-existing file, and the latter is simply pending this human/Superboss audit comment, not a code defect. Tier2 is correctly assigned because the diff touches src/app/api/auth/** and a service-role Supabase client. Approved as sound and ready for human sign-off; not mergeable by this process per tier2 policy.
issues: The diff object supplied for this review was a tracking-file status update only and did not contain the real code change -- reviewers should not rely on the dispatch diff alone for this task and should always pull the referenced PR directly, per the anti-self-report rule in SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md.

Metadata Index Coverage Check is failing on this PR, but it also fails identically on main (unrelated file ai-os/scripts/recover-failed-workers.py) -- pre-existing repo issue, not caused by this change, but flagging since it's a red check a human merger will see.
